➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

​
“The firm response of Iran’s Navy and the intelligent management of the straits demonstrate a shift in the regional balance of power,” Irani stressed.
​
He said the determination of Iran’s Armed Forces, contrary to the expectations of their adversaries, stemmed from “an inseparable bond between faith, the nation and the military.”
​
Irani said that protecting the Persian Gulf and ensuring the security of strategic straits remained a red line and a sacred duty.
​
He added that the mission would be pursued with determination and strength at all times.

In short, the Riemann Hypothesis describes a fundamental pattern in the distribution of prime numbers. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, and the Clay Mathematics Institute offers $1 million for its solution.

The proof has not yet been officially accepted. However, the published materials have already undergone several serious independent technical reviews. If the mathematical community confirms the result, it would be a historic event.

But what matters more here is not the mathematics itself.

If AI really helped solve a problem in just a few weeks that generations of the world's best mathematicians had unsuccessfully worked on for more than a century and a half, it means we're approaching a point where artificial intelligence is beginning to do more than just use existing knowledge — it's starting to create new knowledge.

Now imagine that the next step happens within AI itself.

Today, solving some complex problem might require, say, 10,000 GPUs. Tomorrow, AI discovers a new algorithm that allows it to solve the same problem using 100 GPUs. Then 10. Then just one.

This is still a hypothetical scenario. But if AI really starts independently finding ways to radically improve the efficiency of its own computations, a huge portion of today's forecasts for data centers, energy, and chip demand could quickly become irrelevant.

We're currently building hundreds of billions of dollars' worth of infrastructure based on how much computing power today's technologies require.

But what if tomorrow's technology suddenly requires 100 or 1,000 times less?

And what would happen to all the investments that the market today considers almost guaranteed winners of the AI revolution?
